preamble: In Tehrani Persian, where the historical letters ghayn and qaf have merged into one phoneme /ɢ/, the voiced uvular plosive is realized as a voiced fricative between vowels when unstressed, either velar [ɣ] or uvular [ʁ], and as the stop [ɢ] elsewhere. The intervocalic spirantization is accompanied by optional fronting from uvular to velar place.

examples.note: Intervocalic unstressed /ɢ/ is realized as velar [ɣ] or uvular [ʁ]; word-initially, after consonants and in other strong positions it remains [ɢ], as in قوی‌تر 'stronger' with initial [ɢ].

sources: Majidi, M.-R., & Ternes, E. (1999). Persian (Farsi). In Handbook of the International Phonetic Association. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/9780511807954
